title: Readers’ Rides: Kyle from Outer Shell’s Pop Punk Mall Goth Indy Fab
content:
Hot Topic. Eyeliner. Checkerboard. Kyle from Outer Shell pulled together one sweet Indy Fab with a goth girl theme straight from the mall for this week’s Readers’ Rides…

When I saw the stars on this bike, I had stars in my eyes. The black-to-grey fade and spooky font are so cool and brought me back to growing up at the mall in 7th grade.

We all wanted to look cool cause that made us feel cool. I guess I was a poser, but now as an adult, I think that’s just totally fine. I mean, is it really that bad to want to look cool? I think a lot of people still want that, but we’re told it’s shallow, frivolous – and to ‘grow up’. Maybe being true to yourself is just acknowledging you want to look cool. So, is being a poser actually not being a poser??? Just encouraging others out there – don’t be afraid to accessorize, glamourize, and romanticize.

This bike is an ode to the early 2000’s – Avril Lavigne, Blink 182, Spirit Halloween, mall goths and black nail polish.

A little more detail about the bike. It was custom-made for a person who I think has loved it for a very long time. I bought it second-hand. It was probably made in the late 90s, given the quill stem and groupset. It’s mostly a CX bike, but with touring add-ons like triple bottle cages, fender mounts, and front and rear rack mounts.

The 3×9 drivetrain works great. It’s affordable and gives me a better gear range than anything I can buy today. I had Paul Components build me brake levers to match the black and silver finish of the XT group. Also, Tyler from BTCHN’ bikes built me some awesome Ti handlebars based on a mood board I sent him. It’s anodized with Goosebumps-inspired drips and scene queen-inspired checkers. Wow.

The front rack and bag combination were big considerations as well. I’ve been wanting this carry system for my daily commute, so I might have built an entirely new bike around it. I DO like to build bikes based on the bags they go with… You may notice the extra adapter plate on the rack. That’s part of our new Fidlock Tote attachment system I’ve been prototyping. Of course, I had to have matching straps on the bag and a custom hand-stitched leather doll from Pretty Popular Studio.

For the top tube pad, I used a polished nickel zipper with DIY distressed canvas. I discovered you can separate out the warp of the fabric and cut them out, leaving the weft strands still attached. A little sandpaper and it looks just like pants from Hot Topic! To top it off, I also made a custom tiny tie and added some studded bracelets.

Yes, my bike has an outfit that isn’t practical. Bikes don’t have to be, and neither do you.

Build Spec

  • Frame: Independent Fabrications CX/Touring Custom
  • Wheelset: Sun Rhyno Lite with Deore XT M750
  • Handlebar: BTCHN’ Ti FlatBar 16 with Custom Anodizing
  • Bar Ends: HEX Components
  • Stem: Nitto Dynamic 11
  • Grips: ODI Cult x Vans Waffle
  • Seatpost: SunTour XC Comp
  • Saddle: Selle Italia Flite with Anodized Ti Rails
  • Groupset: Deore XT M750 3×9
  • Brake Levers: Paul Canti
  • Brakes: Paul Minimoto
  • Pedals: MKS Gamma
  • Tires: Panaracer Urban Max
  • Rack: Rat King RIP
  • Bag: Outer Shell Fidlock Tote
  • Bracelets: Hot Topic
  • Top Tube Pad: Outer Shell Custom
  • Tie: Outer Shell Custom
